Formulation
Patient presents with acute, non-mental health-related gastrointestinal symptoms characterized by diarrhea lasting three days with associated mild abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting. Past medical history of asthma and family history significant for father’s hypertension and bowel cancer. No mental health issues or psychosocial stressors identified in the consultation. Patient exhibits adequate hydration and no signs of severe systemic illness at time of assessment.

- Patient Goal(s): Not applicable
- Clinical Goal(s): Not applicable
- Actions (Patient): Monitor symptoms, maintain hydration, follow dietary advice
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide education on soft diet and symptom management, advise on when to seek urgent care, monitor for worsening symptoms

- Not applicable

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Soft diet advice, hydration importance, signs warranting stool sample/testing or hospital admission (increased stool frequency, blood in stool, dehydration), over-the-counter options like Dioralyte
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Passage of blood in stool, diarrhea > 8 times/day, persistent diarrhea > 1 week, dehydration symptoms
- Coping Strategies: Dietary modifications, use of probiotics (yogurts), use of oral rehydration solutions
